readings: The models are small (depth 4, 16.9 M and 34.7 M parameters) and this is one corpus family at one recipe. A reading is about the two widths and two rates on these draws. No reading claims a mechanism or a scaling law, and nothing about Jane Street's scale follows.
P1 has a reading on 6 of 6 draws; without one: none.
Draws without a reading, by statistic (undefined fit, target outside the path, draw missing): P1 0, 0, 0; S1 0, 0, 0; S3 0, 0, 0; S4 0, 0, 0; S5 0, 0, 0; S2 0, 3, 0.

At 1e-4, p* at 512 at E3 is above p* at 768 read at the training NLL 512 reaches at E3 (REVERSAL_CONFIRMED). At fixed updates at E3 on these draws, 768 is above 512, so on these draws the comparison axis reverses the 512-768 ordering at 1e-4. This does not show a capacity mechanism, and nothing about Jane Street's scale follows. Matching on training loss also removes any faster learning of the wider model, so neither axis is privileged.
S1, at 1e-4, matched on the gap: CONFIRMED. At 1e-4, p* at 512 at E3 is above p* at 768 read at the gap 512 reaches at E3.

S3, at 1e-4, the fixed-update contrast at E3: CONFIRMED. S3 replicates N6's fixed-budget result (RATE_DEPENDENT): after 3,072 updates at 1e-4, 768 is above 512. This is a fixed-budget fact. It does not say that the fall from 512 to 768 depends on the rate.
S4, at 3e-4, matched on training NLL: CONFIRMED. At 3e-4, p* at 512 at E3 is above p* at 768 read at the training NLL 512 reaches at E3.
S5, at 3e-4, the fixed-update contrast at E3: CONFIRMED. At 3e-4, after 3,072 updates, 512 is above 768, as in N6. This is a fixed-budget fact.
S2, at 1e-4, matched on validation NLL: UNAVAILABLE. It is not read.

Data: never-assigned WikiText-103 training articles, excluding every article of N5 and N6 and their text duplicates and repeats inside the pool; new seeds; no new tuning. The validation set, the pre-training pool and the tokenizer are those of the earlier natural-text studies. The hypothesis came from a post-hoc reanalysis of N6 (reports/adversarial-review-20261104-01/RECOMPUTE_MATCHED.json), so N6 cannot confirm it. p* between readouts is a linear interpolation over a quarter of an epoch. A draw whose target lies outside 768's E2-E3.5 path is unavailable for that statistic, and such draws are not a random subset. Equal training NLL is not equal gain, because p* is fit to gains from each width's own E0. The t intervals assume normal draws, untested at five or six.
note: P1 is the pre-registered primary; S1 to S5 are read as confirmations only as the fixed sequence allows, and a step it does not reach has the label NOT_READ, with the side of its interval in its status; NOT_OVERFIT, the leave-one-out intervals, the sign tests and every other section are reported and do not gate.
